mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 YoY growth is below -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and dampens earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals broad-based demand deterioration, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below its long-run average and CPI inflation rises above 2% for three consecutive months, monetary policy is likely too loose relative to inflation, which erodes real yields and supports S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < long-run average AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below its long-run average and CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its previous peak signals a recovery in aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4%).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds previous peak AND CPIAUCSL <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 exceeds its previous peak and CPIAUCSL is not above 4%.
